risks.title: Intense competition in hearing aids and implants market
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions the need to offer 'the most innovative hearing solutions' facing a market requiring a broad range of solutions, with structural competitive pressure in a sector dominated by few global players (Demant, WS Audiology, GN Audio). The trend is stable but intensifies with emergence of OTC hearing aids.

risks.title: Dependence on institutional reimbursement and insurance policies
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly states that 'the cost of hearing care is generally shared between the consumer and an institutional reimbursement regime or insurance' and that 'pricing is therefore highly dependent on policies of these regimes'. This dependence is central to the business model and exposes Sonova to administrative decisions outside its control.

risks.title: Medical device regulatory risk and approvals
risks.score_rationale: Sonova markets hearing aids and cochlear implants classified as medical devices subject to strict regulations (FDA, CE MDR, etc.) in over 100 countries. Intensifying regulatory requirements (e.g. EU MDR transition) represent significant operational and financial risk implicitly mentioned in the multi-country context.

risks.title: Intellectual property protection and counterfeiting risk
risks.score_rationale: The document highlights that Sonova holds 2,082 active patents and design rights and filed 52 new applications in 2023/24, signaling strategic IP importance. In a competitive technology sector, counterfeiting or patent invalidation litigation risk is structurally high.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and health data protection
risks.score_rationale: The document describes mobile applications collecting continuous health data ('health measurements, continuous data monitoring'), remote adjustments of cochlear implants and hearing aids via digital platforms. These sensitive medical data flows constitute prime targets for cyberattacks, with major regulatory implications (GDPR, HIPAA).

risks.title: Acquisition integration risk in Audiological Care
risks.score_rationale: The document mentions 'several acquisitions of small companies' in EMEA, United States, Americas and Asia/Pacific during 2023/24, bringing the network to over 3,600 clinics in 20 countries. Growth through multiple acquisitions generates recurring operational, cultural and systems integration risks.

risks.title: Shortage of qualified hearing care professionals
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly identifies 'lack of educational infrastructure in many countries' as a barrier to hearing care access, and describes significant investments (SIHA, Sonova Academy) to train professionals. This structural shortage directly affects Sonova's distribution capacity and growth ability.

risks.title: Emergence of OTC hearing aids and distribution model disruption
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions the launch of OTC hearing aids in the United States, purchasable online or in retail and self-adjustable, representing a rupture from the traditional prescriber-professional model. This regulatory and commercial disruption is recent (FDA OTC ruling 2022) and its impact on product mix and margins is under evaluation.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or AI solutions in the 2023/24 annual report. The company emphasizes product innovation in audiology, audiological research and sustainability, without reference to AI as a strategic lever. Cited innovations are based on universal Bluetooth connectivity and technical improvement.
evidence: No occurrence of 'artificial intelligence', 'AI', 'machine learning' or 'deep learning' in the document.
Cited innovations (Lumity, Remote Programming, SmartSpeech Technology, AutoSense OS) are based on Bluetooth connectivity and audiological technical improvement, not AI.
Partnerships, R&D and features do not mention AI algorithms or machine learning.
